explanation.text: The HTTP status code for a disallowed known method is 405, as defined in RFC 9110 and recorded by IANA in 2022.
The HTTP status code for an unimplemented method is 501, as defined in RFC 9110 and recorded by IANA in 2022.
The value 405 is lower than 501, contradicting the claim that the disallowed method code is higher.
RFC 9110, which defines standard HTTP status codes in 2022, supports the assignment of 405 for Method Not Allowed and 501 for Not Implemented.
A server returns 405 when a method is recognized but not allowed, and 501 when the method is not implemented or unrecognized.
The claim that the disallowed method code is higher than the unimplemented method code is false because 405 is numerically less than 501.

excerpts.text: The HTTP **`501 Not Implemented`** [server error response](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Status#server_error_responses) status code means that the server does not support the functionality required to fulfill the request.
`501` is the appropriate response when the server does not recognize the request method and is incapable of supporting it for any resource.
If the server does recognize the method, but intentionally does not allow it, the appropriate response is [`405 Method Not Allowed`](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Status/405).
